LESSON: HUMAN RIGHTS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Systems
Topic 4.4: Human rights

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Human rights. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How could respect for human rights promote unity in society?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain classification of human rights in society
2. describe ways in which human rights are upheld in society
3. demonstrate ways in which human rights are upheld in society
4. explain the causes of conflicts in society today
5. describe peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in society
6. value peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HUMAN RIGHTS
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Human rights helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: HUMAN RIGHTS
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain classification of human rights in society

What this means
In this part you learn to explain classification of human rights in society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain classification of human rights in society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Human rights” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain classification of human rights in society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe ways in which human rights are upheld in society

What this means
In this part you learn to describe ways in which human rights are upheld in society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe ways in which human rights are upheld in society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Human rights.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe ways in which human rights are upheld in society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Demonstrate ways in which human rights are upheld in society

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate ways in which human rights are upheld in society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate ways in which human rights are upheld in society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate ways in which human rights are upheld in society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Explain the causes of conflicts in society today

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the causes of conflicts in society today. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the causes of conflicts in society today.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Human rights” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the causes of conflicts in society today. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Describe peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in society

What this means
In this part you learn to describe peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Human rights.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 6: Value peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in society

What this means
In this part you learn to value peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Human rights is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Human rights” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain classification of human rights in society)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Human rights. (skill: describe ways in which human rights are upheld in society)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: demonstrate ways in which human rights are upheld in society)

Example 4: Connect “Human rights” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain the causes of conflicts in society today)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Human rights to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain classification of human rights in society.
3. Practise this skill: describe ways in which human rights are upheld in society.
4. Practise this skill: demonstrate ways in which human rights are upheld in society.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Human rights from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Human rights: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Human rights?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How could respect for human rights promote unity in society?
2. Why should we embrace peaceful co-existence in society?
3. How can we live peacefully with others in society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Human rights means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain classification of human rights in society.
5. Be able to: describe ways in which human rights are upheld in society.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
